sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Messiah University and Calvin University are both private nonprofit institutions, with Messiah located in Mechanicsburg and Calvin in Grand Rapids. Messiah University has an undergraduate enrollment of 2,259 students, while Calvin University enrolls 3,193 undergraduates. Tuition for in-state students at Messiah is $42,240, which is higher compared to Calvin's $39,350. These differences highlight variations in size, location, and cost between Messiah vs Calvin.

sections.heading: Cost

Messiah University charges $42,240 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition, whereas Calvin University’s tuition is $39,350 for both categories. Regarding student debt, the median debt for graduates who complete their programs at Messiah is $25,621, slightly higher than Calvin’s median debt of $23,250. These figures illustrate the financial differences between Messiah vs Calvin, reflecting variations in tuition pricing and student borrowing.

Overall, Messiah vs Calvin shows that Messiah University has a higher tuition cost and median debt among completers compared to Calvin University. These cost factors are important considerations for prospective students evaluating their educational investment at either institution.
